And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

Den 6 juni 1944 landsteg 156 000 amerikanska, brittiska och kanadensiska trupper på en fyrtiofem kilometers strandremsa i Normandie i Frankrike. Efter flera månader av intensivt kamper övervann de de inledande försvaren och strömmade in i territorium som hölls av tyskarna. Överraskningsanfallet, känt som D‑dagen, fångade tyskarna oförberedda. Det var dock inte förrän i mars året därpå som Frankrike slutligen befriades från de tyska styrkorna. D‑dagen var början på slutet för andra världskriget vid västfronten och det händelseförlopp som tycktes suga ur livet ur den beryktade tyska armén, från vilken de aldrig hämtade sig. Det förefaller i högsta grad sammanträffande att så många ord med negativ klang börjar på bokstaven D: besvikelse, tvivel, sorgsenhet, undergång, desillusion, nedslagenhet, dyster, nederlag, förtvivlan, depression, förtvivlan, ödeläggelse, bedrägeri och död.

Jag kan föreställa mig att dessa två troende, vacklande på vägen till Emmaus den där dunkla och dystra aftonen, kände sig ungefär likadant. Deras D‑dag hade anlänt helt oväntat. Jag skulle misstänka att varje levande människa vid något tillfälle upplevt stunder av intensiv sorg—sin egen D‑dag, så att säga. Även några djur har känt sorg vid sin ägares eller partners död. Men dessa två lärjungar verkade utstå en smärta långt bortom den normala sorg över en vän. De stirrade in i den hårda verkligheten att alla deras ljusa hopp om en strålande morgondag var hopplöst krossade i en ruinös hög vid korsets fot.

Denna ångest var ingen vanlig depression utan snarare en depression knuten till en troskris. Denna typ av nedstämdhet är ett tillstånd av intensiv andlig plåga där den kämpande, förtvivlade troende känner sig övergiven av Gud. Det är en hopplös känsla av att Guds välsignelsens sol har förmörkats och själens mörka natt blivit en permanent gäst inom.

Medan vi alla strävar efter att tappert motstå sådana mörka frestelser, visar en kort genomgång av många gudfryktiga männens liv att dessa frestelser är mycket verkliga och ganska vanliga för människan. I ett sådant tillstånd synes livet omöjligt och den förestående dysterhet som lagt sig över hjärtat ser inget ljus i slutet av tunneln. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. Detta är uppenbarligen en överdriven förstoring som undslapp den gråtande profetens läppar, men den ger oss en direkt ögonblicksbild av den fruktade smärtan djupt i hans själ.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. Denna själens mörka natt visar ingen hänsyn till personer. Den invaderar liv hos furstar och fattiga, predikanter och ångerfyllda, offentliga och privata människor, predikstolar och bänkar. Dessa två lärjungar hade muntligt gått igenom varje möjlig scenarie på sin vandring längs Emmausvägen. De hade utan tvekan funnit många fel hos andra samt personlig ånger. De ”tänk om” och ”om bara” hade noggrant diskuterats, men inget kunde återkalla utfallet och deras rastlösa oro bestod fortfarande.

Vägen från Jerusalem till Emmaus var about threescore furlongs eller ungefär sju miles. Och längs denna bedrövliga färd anslöt sig en Främling till det plågade paret i deras D‑dag och frågade dem om orsaken till deras sorg. Men han är ingen nyfiken åskådare. Han är den uppståndne Herre som kommit för att kasta sitt himmelska ljus över vår förmörkade stig. Istället för att uppenbara sig plötsligt, och kanske för vår skull, tillåter han tålmodigt att de blottlägger den uttömda andliga väg de trampade på.

Så utvecklar sig samtalet medan milstenarna passerar, och var och en avslöjar våra ärliga felaktiga ansträngningar som leder oss längre bort från fridens stad och in i själens mörka natt…

…Andras okunnighet

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Fråga vilken främling som helst på New Yorks gator varför flaggorna vajade på halv stång tre dagar efter att tornen föll den 11 september, och du skulle få samma häpna svar som dessa två. ”Hur kan du vara så okunnig?” Vi har alla en tendens att förundras över människor som inte besitter samma kunskap som vi föreställer oss. Ju yngre mannen är, desto fler svar tror han att hans förståelses kistor rymmer.

Detta är inget nytt. Moses, som ung man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. Medan han bestämt förstod att han hade Guds plan, tog han fel beträffande hur stor del han verkligen hade. Om vårt återtåg inte kan rätta till den givna situationen är våra svar inte det verkliga svaret. Den innerliga förakt som naturligen uppstår mot dem som ser det annorlunda är början på att vi är på fel väg. Mil efter mil längs livets väg började Moses känna desperationens smärta och timmens mörker. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Varför såg inte Moses detta tidigare i livet? Av samma orsak som dessa två brinnande lärjungars …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Förnuftet

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. De hade sin privata uppfattning om vem Kristus var, men de såg …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Deras delvisa kunskap lutade tungt mot deras eget förstånd och de sökte efter fel sorts befrielse. För dem var deras frälsare (i dåtid) en profet som inte längre kunde göra vad de ville att han skulle göra. Vi vill alla att Jesus ska lösa våra problem och få oss att må bättre, men Hans syfte är att befria oss från vår förmodan och synd.

Jakob hade all orsak att tro att förstfödslorätten och välsignelsen skulle bli hans. I Betel hade Gud lovat att välsigna honom. Jakob föreställde sig att detta skulle komma i materiell form. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

Men den största välsignelse han någonsin mottog från Gud kom till honom på vingar av en djup mörk natt. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jakob hade redan samlat en rikedom av jordiska ägodelar. Vad mer kunde han begära? Det var en mörk natt för Jakob när han upptäckte att han spenderat sitt liv på att jaga ägodelar och motstå Gud. Nu söker han gudfruktig karaktär och andlig rikedom. Hans seger kom genom överlåtelse, och han haltade därifrån som en krympling med en krona. Herren kan inte fullständigt välsigna en människa förrän Han först har erövrat dennes förnuftets makter.

…Olycklig lott

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. Gud är specialist på att vända gravallvarliga dilemma till monumentala segrar. Ändå ser människan sig omkring och förbannar mörkret omkring sig. Fastän det kan finnas en kaskad av gott som återgäldar dem, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. Att ge överdriven tyngd åt det onda omkring oss är att håna Guds gudomlighet. Medan vi alla kan ångra saker vi kunde ha gjort eller sagt annorlunda, måste vi oundvikligen lämna resultaten i Guds händer. Job upplevde lika mycket olycka som någon annan. Så mycket att han öppnade …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. Men någonstans innan de mörka händelserna rättades till och lyftes kom ljuset in i hans själ, och han lade sin hand mot sin mun och tillbad.

…Egen agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. Det är helt naturligt att försöka förstå en given situation och dessa två hade valt rätt ekvation. Deras dumhet låg i antagandet om de medel genom vilka Kristus skulle utföra detta och vilken typ av befrielse de skulle få. De såg fram emot den dag då deras nation skulle lyftas över romarna. När vi omedvetet söker vår egen trygghet leder det oundvikligen till bitter besvikelse. Naaman föreställde sig …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham hade fått löfte om Kanaans land och bad om en bekräftelse. Han förberedde då det förbundsoffer som Gud föreskrev, men hela dagen gick och Gud gjorde ingenting med dem. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

När Abraham väntade på att Gud skulle ta emot hans offer fortsatte han att slå bort rovdjuren. Men när dagen närmade sig sitt slut började han känna sig övergiven av Gud och nattens mörker började lägga sig över hans själ. Det krävs en midnattsupplevelse för att det ska bli tillräckligt mörkt för att vi ska kunna se stjärnorna och tillräckligt tyst för att höra Hans röst. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Otålighet

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Många av oss är tillräckligt disciplinerade för att hålla ut en tid. Det är när vårt hopp fördröjs (see Proverbs 13:12) som våra hjärtan blir sjuka och försvagas. Tre dagar verkade lång tid för dessa två. Men tre dagar, veckor, månader, år eller till och med årtionden ligger alla inom Guds klockas räckvidd. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Josef uthärdade tålmodigt sina bröders och Potifars misshandel, men fängelset blev långt, och han bad kammarherren att befordra honom när han återfått sin ställning. Men det var two full years (Genesis 41:1) innan Farao drömde och Josef slutligen kallades fram. Men det var inte så mycket kammarherren som var skyldig som Guds vilja, som kallat Josef att vara …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. Det finns ingen mer effektiv väg att lära oss tålamod än mörkrets disciplin, från vilken få helgon är undantagna.

…Självömkan

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. Ingen tycker om att missa något. Faktum är att psykologin upptäckt en ny störning—FOMO (fear of missing out). Budskapet som kvinnorna förde var goda nyheter och en fantastisk vändning, ändå gav det de andra ingen glädje för det hade inte hänt dem. Goda nyheter har sällan genomträngande kraft i en person insvept i självömkan, och Elia var en sådan. Hans mörka natt kom i kölvattnet av en hisnande triumf på Karmelberget mot Baals profeter. Men i sitt eget inre mörker …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Känslor av misslyckande

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. Det är lätt att tänka, ”Det fungerade för dem men det fungerar inte för mig.” Medan misslyckade ansträngningar kan nedslå oss, är det inte nödvändigtvis ett misslyckande från vår sida. Johannes Döparen hade troget kallat folket till omvändelse, döpt Kristus och vittnat om den dånande rösten från himlen. Han förkunnade korrekt den kommande Messias och pekade sina lärjungar mot …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. Denna tjänst gav honom en säker plats i en mörk fängelsehåla. Han hade blivit väl van vid brist på tröst och spär kost, men det var känslan av fullständig övergivenhet av Gud som förde honom in i mörka tvivel. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

”Hade jag fel?” I mörkret började han uppleva livet på frågetecknets sluttande rygg. John Bunyan beskriver det som förtvivlans gyttja. Det kan förefalla som D‑dagen för den kristne, men överdriven betoning på våra misslyckade ansträngningar främjar ingen uppståndelse.

Slutsats

Inte allt andligt mörker är helt undvikbart. Inte varje andlig upplevelse är en tid av innerlig välsignelse, och inte varje plats är det heller. Det finns tider av förföljelse och prövning som är avsedda att föra de heliga till en själens uppgörelse som endast mörka nätter kan uträtta. Jesus själv frestades på ett liknande sätt som vi, när i den genomträngande mörkret vid den nionde timmen på korset, hans röst ljöd …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

Vägen till Emmaus vittnar om det faktum att ett levande trosliv inte ger någon garanti för frånvaron av andlig depression. Det är en berättelse om verkliga människor med verklig tro som upplever verkliga prövningar. Det lär oss att även andliga njutningar inte bör hållas för hårt. Våra trygga visioner för framtiden, både omedelbara och långsiktiga, måste doppas i ödmjukhetens eld. Den mörka natten är platsen där sådan självbedrägeri dör, och en intim kännedom om Gud föds. Den förvandlar oss från att älska Gud för de välsignelser Han ger oss, till att älska Gud för vår relation med Honom och gemenskapen som följer.

Resesällskapet till Kleopas nämndes aldrig vid namn. Vissa tror att det var hans hustru. Andra hävdar att det var Lukas. Men deras identitet utelämnades, kanske för att vi lättare ska fylla tomrummet med våra egna namn. Sju miles från Jerusalem snubblar vi över den skarpa verkligheten om vem Frälsaren verkligen är och att frälsning är mer än bara ett stämpligt intyg på tillhörighet. Skalen faller från våra ögon och själens mörka natt ger vika för middagens ljus av Guds närvaro. Det är då vi gör vår glädjerusning tillbaka till fridens stad endast för att bli missförstådda igen. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

Och så undrar jag till och med över nyttan av att skriva ner sådana tankar. Det är ingen upplevelse som kan framställas eller intellektuellt förstås. Det är en högt personlig sammankomst med Gud och skräddarsydd speciellt för varje individ. Men kanske kan vi, i vår grunda generation, uppmuntras att nå ut och omfamna mörkret i stället för att möta det med avsky och motstånd. Och där i nattens hotfulla mörker, lära oss att omfamna ljusets Frälsare.

Länge låg min fångna ande,
Fast bunden i synd och naturens natt.
Din blick spred en livgivande stråle,
Jag vaknade; fängelset flammande i ljus.
Mina bojor föll. Mitt hjärta var fritt.
Jag reste mig, gick ut och följde Dig.

- Charles Wesley

There is coming a day when all will be well.
The things that are bad will all be in hell.
But we must not forget that day has not come.
We are in a battle; we must still overcome.
The enemy rages, his time here is short.
He spreads all his lies, the truth to distort.
Sin in our lives, it is his great goal.
For he knows very well it will cost us our soul.
It need not be big; a small sin will do.
He’ll trick and deceive, each soul to pursue.
The darts of the wicked come from all sides.
When faced with God’s power, that devil—he hides!
When God is with us, he cannot advance!
When God is with us, sin has no chance!
For the eyes of the Lord seek to and fro,
To find one perfect, His power He’ll show!
Let’s be done with the lesser and look far beyond.
Let’s take hold of God’s power! It’s time to respond!

","section":null,"subtitle":null,"title":"The Battle That Rages"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"location":null,"name":"Barry Grant"}],"raw":"–by Barry Grant"}},"target_language":"Norwegian (Bokmål)","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Det kommer en dag når alt blir godt.
Det som er ondt, vil være i rov og rot.
Men vi må ikke glemme at dagen ennå ikke er her.
Vi kjemper i strid; vi må vise mot og være nær.
Fienden raser, hans tid her er kort.
Han sprer alle løgner for å forvrenge vårt ord.
Synd i våre liv er hans store mål.
For han vet svært godt at den kan røve vår sjel så sår.
Det trenger ikke være stort; en liten synd vil du se.
Han lurer og bedrar for hver sjel å få med.
De onde piler kommer fra alle kanter.
Når han møter Guds kraft, da flykter hans tanker!
Når Gud er med oss, kan han ikke gå frem!
Når Gud er med oss, har synden ingen hjem!
For Herrens øyne leter hit og dit,
For å finne en fullkommen — Hans kraft vil bli vist!
La oss gi slipp på det små og se langt forbi.

This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.

Este es el primero de una serie de artículos sobre “Discipulado”. Hoy, Jesús continúa llamando a hombres y mujeres a responder al simple llamado: “Sígueme”. Jesús está llamando a cada uno de nosotros a “seguirle” personalmente. En esta serie exploraremos la profundidad de este simple mandato de Jesús. Como los discípulos, te sentirás atraído a seguir a Jesús.

Puedes experimentar tanto exaltación como aprensión. Exaltación, cuando tu camino de fe te lleva a alturas de amor que nunca habías conocido. Aprensión, cuando tu fe es probada de maneras nuevas y difíciles.

Hay un vacío en todo corazón humano que sólo Jesús puede llenar. Hay una pureza y belleza en la vida de Jesús que resuena con esos anhelos del corazón. Al caminar con Jesús, nos hallamos siendo transformados. Lo viejo pasa. Todas las cosas se hacen nuevas. Su vida se convierte en nuestra vida. Sus deseos se convierten en nuestros deseos.

El discipulado es incumbente al creyente. Creer en Jesús, arrepentirse de nuestros pecados y recibir al Señor Jesús en nuestro corazón son los primeros pasos hacia un viaje de fe de toda la vida. El discipulado no es un medio alternativo de salvación. Seguir a Jesús es la respuesta de un alma liberada. Seguir a Jesús no es un intento carnal de merecer la vida eterna. Es la respuesta de amor de quien ha descubierto la fuente de la vida.

Si te unes a nosotros en este camino, descubrirás que seguir a Jesús nos conducirá al valle de la decisión donde nos veremos compelidos a escoger entre una vida de entrega total a Cristo o una vida de pecado y complacencia propia.

Y Jesús, andando junto al mar de Galilea, vio a dos hermanos, Simón que se llama Pedro, y Andrés su hermano, echando la red en el mar; porque eran pescadores. Y les dice: Venid en pos de mí, y haré que seáis pescadores de hombres. Y ellos, luego, dejando las redes, le siguieron. Y yendo de allí, vio a otros dos hermanos, Jacobo hijo de Zebedeo, y Juan su hermano, en la barca con Zebedeo su padre, remendando las redes; y los llamó. Y luego ellos, dejando la barca y a su padre, le siguieron –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagínate en una barca con uno de esos hermanos. El sol se levantaba en el horizonte oriental. Anticipando otro día de pesca en las azules aguas de la Galilea, te ocupas en las tareas diarias. La pesca ha sido tu vida. Estás tan a gusto en el mar como en tu cabaña.

Otro día, otra captura de peces, y deberías poder mantener a raya a los acreedores por otra semana. Es la única vida que has conocido. Tu padre fue pescador. Tu abuelo fue pescador. Es una vida cómoda. Es una vida familiar.

Esta mañana, mientras las olas acarician suavemente la orilla arenosa, se acerca un hombre. No es un perfecto desconocido. Todos saben del hijo de María. Todos tienen una opinión sobre el hijo de María. Asombra al rabino local con su conocimiento de las Escrituras. Su carácter es impecable; es amigo de todos y extraño para ninguno.

Este hombre, Jesús (ese es su nombre) se aproxima a tu barca. Al acercarse, llama en una voz bastante alegre: “Sígueme”.

Jacobo mira a Juan, y juntos miran a su padre Zebedeo. Su asentimiento aprobatorio fue todo lo que necesitaban. Zebedeo había trabajado con sus dos hijos por muchos años. Quizás esperaba que el tiempo con el nazareno ablandara el temperamento de sus caracteres ásperos.

“Sígueme, y yo os haré pescadores de hombres.” Eso fue lo que gritó a Pedro y a Andrés. Ellos dejaron su pequeña barca llena de redes, quizás atada a un tronco en la orilla. ¿Qué había en este Hombre que podía atraer discípulos tras Él con un simple “Sígueme”? Tal vez fue un anhelo profundo en el corazón de estos discípulos—una “esperanza” de que seguir a Jesús podría cumplirla.

Generaciones de hombres judíos habían esperado al Mesías—Al Prometido; Aquel que rompería el yugo romano y restauraría a Israel a su antigua libertad y gloria. Jesús era la perspectiva revolucionaria más prometedora del día. Necesitaría seguidores. Necesitaría su ayuda. Poco se daban cuenta aquel día, al dejar sus redes y seguir a Jesús, adónde los llevaría ese camino. Poco imaginaban que si seguían a este Hombre, nunca serían los mismos.

Cuando Pedro, Andrés, Jacobo y Juan se unieron con otros ocho para seguir a Jesús, estaban abandonando la vida conocida y segura del pescador. Podían pensar que seguir a Jesús sería una aventura. Podían pensar que después de un periodo de servicio al nazareno, podrían regresar a sus barcas de pesca. De hecho, eso fue lo que hicieron.

Después de la crucifixión y resurrección de Jesús, Él se manifestó varias veces a sus discípulos. Aún no habían recibido el Espíritu Santo y, en medio de esa gran incertidumbre, no pudieron resistir el atractivo de lo familiar. Decidieron ir a pescar, pero para su consternación habían perdido la mano. Pescaron toda la noche y no atraparon nada. Por la mañana Jesús estaba de pie en la orilla. Les dijo que arrojaran la red al lado derecho de la barca. La arrojaron y no pudieron tirar de las redes por la multitud de peces.

Simón Pedro les dice: Voy a pescar. Le dicen: Vamos también nosotros contigo. Salieron y entraron en la barca inmediatamente, y aquella noche no cogieron nada. Pero cuando ya amanecía, se presentó Jesús en la playa; mas los discípulos no sabían que era Jesús. Entonces Jesús les dijo: Hijitos, ¿tenéis algo de comer? Le respondieron: No. Y él les dijo: Echad la red a la derecha de la barca, y hallaréis. Entonces la echaron, y ya no podían sacarla por la multitud de peces –John 21:3-6.

¿Te has encontrado alguna vez en una situación en la que lo intentas una y otra vez y todos tus esfuerzos se encuentran con el fracaso? Sabes lo que es “llegar al fin de mis recursos acumulados”. Si es ahí donde te hallas, estás en posición de experimentar un milagro. Dios se muestra fuerte a los que reconocen su debilidad.

Cuando decides seguir a Jesús, Él te atraerá a tal dependencia absoluta de Él que finalmente ya no confiarás en ti mismo. Llegar a ser verdaderamente como Jesús es darse cuenta, con Pablo, …que en mí (esto es, en mi carne) no mora el bien… Pablo continúa el versículo …porque el querer está en mí, pero el cómo efectuar lo bueno no lo hallo –Romans 7:18.

El discipulado nos conducirá a un abandono total de nosotros mismos a Cristo. Así como los discípulos no pudieron concebir adónde los llevaría seguir a Jesús, tampoco nosotros podemos. Tomamos una decisión de fe. Elegimos seguir. Confiamos los detalles a nuestro Maestro.

Si quieres ser como Jesús, no puedes mirar atrás. Jesús dijo: …Ninguno que puso la mano en el arado y mira atrás, es apto para el reino de Dios –Luke 9:62. Pedro miró atrás. Dijo: “Voy a pescar”. Desilusionado tras la crucifixión y la gloriosa resurrección, Pedro escogió volver al estilo de vida que le era familiar. Volvió a pescar y Jacobo y Juan fueron con él.

Cuando Jesús apareció en la orilla después de su larga noche de trabajo infructuoso, preparó una fritura de pescado para los discípulos cansados. Mientras Pedro masticaba un pescado asado, Jesús se volvió hacia él y dijo: “Pedro, ¿me amas más que éstos?” Qué palabras tan suavemente penetrantes las de Jesús.

Pedro respondió: “Sí, Señor, tú sabes que te amo.” Jesús dijo: “Apacienta mis corderos.” No sabemos cuánto tiempo pasó, pero Jesús se volvió a él otra vez, “Pedro…” (en realidad lo llamó Simón) “¿me amas?” Pedro dio la misma respuesta acostumbrada. “Sí, Señor, tú sabes que te amo”. Era la respuesta correcta, pero a Jesús le interesaba más que una respuesta correcta, así que le dijo de nuevo: “Simón, hijo de Jonás, ¿me amas?”

Pedro finalmente empezó a sentir que Jesús le pedía algo más—algo que le atravesaba el alma de parte a parte. Había comenzado a seguir a Jesús con el deseo de recibir de Él. Ahora Jesús le está pidiendo que corresponda ese amor.

Se le aparecieron escenas de la casa de Caifás. Vio a Jesús siendo tratado brutalmente, acusado falsamente y escupido. Oyó los gritos airados del Sanedrín pidiendo la muerte de Jesús. Y luego estuvo aquella joven persistente que lo desafió diciendo que él era uno de los discípulos de Jesús. Él le dijo: “No lo soy”. Tres veces negó conocer a Jesús y ahora tres veces Jesús ha desafiado su amor.

En angustia de corazón Pedro clamó: “Señor, tú lo sabes todo; tú sabes que te amo”. Jesús le dijo: “Apacienta mis ovejas”. Desde ese día, Pedro fue un hombre con un llamado, no sólo a conocer a Cristo con el propósito de recibir de él, sino también a emularlo. El discipulado es más que simplemente saber acerca de Jesús. El discipulado es andar en sus pasos e identificarse con Jesús en su ministerio y en sus sufrimientos—conocerle verdaderamente.

Jesús te está preguntando hoy: “¿Me amas?” Todos sabemos la respuesta correcta: “Sí, por supuesto, amo a Jesús.” Entonces “Ama a tu prójimo” – “Sirve a los necesitados” – “Cede a tu hermano” – “Perdona a quien te ha ofendido”.

El discipulado es muy práctico en cuanto nos mueve más allá de lo ideológico y nos hace ser las mismas manos y pies de Jesús para los que nos rodean.

Si en tu corazón piensas, esto no suena muy atractivo, te animaría a que te concentres en el momento y en la tarea presente. Pedro caminó con Jesús durante tres años y medio antes de recibir este llamado de Jesús. Jesús nunca nos llama sin equiparnos, y no nos equipa hasta que determina que estamos listos. Después del día de Pentecostés, Pedro fue llamado, preparado y equipado. Entonces Dios lo usó poderosamente para establecer la iglesia.

Me gustaría llamar tu atención hacia otro atributo del discipulado que a veces se malinterpreta. El discipulado nunca pretende ser tedioso. Si encuentras que seguir a Jesús es duro y trabajoso, eso es evidencia de que tu amor aún no ha sido perfeccionado.

La pregunta que traspasó el alma de Jesús a Pedro fue bastante simple: “¿Me amas?” Era como si Jesús estuviera probando a Pedro. [“Tengo un trabajo para ti, Pedro, pero un requisito previo para este trabajo es tu amor devoto por mí.”] El discipulado es una respuesta de amor a Jesús. Nuestro amor por Cristo hace que el servicio sea una alegría. El trabajo es placentero y el sacrificio no es una pérdida.

Podemos entender esto mejor en el contexto de las relaciones humanas. Ellie edged her chair closer to the grown-ups who were visiting in the kitchen. Grandpa, Grandma, and Aunt Lily had stopped by for a visit, and although she didn’t always understand the conversation, she loved to listen. She found that she learned a lot of things that way.

The topic this evening was about something related to church and that got her mind to thinking about singing during Sunday morning worship services. Although Ellie was only five years old, she very much loved to sing. She thought about the fact that her dear Grandpa was a song leader in their church and how much she liked when he led a song.

At Ellie’s church the song leaders all sat around a table near the center of the church. They took turns choosing a song and then leading it for the congregation. Ellie didn’t always know the songs that were chosen. They sang out of a little black hymnbook that had lots of songs with hard words and tunes she didn’t recognize. However, in the back of this little songbook was a section called “The Appendix” and here were hymns that were familiar to her and she was always pleased when a song was announced from that part of the book. Her favorite song was ‘Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ and although she couldn’t read yet, she knew it was number eight. When that particular song number was announced on a Sunday morning, she always felt a twinge of excitement. She would be able to help along with this song!

I wish we would sing that song again, thought Ellie. It’s been a long time since we have.

Then a sudden thought struck her. Why couldn’t she ask Grandpa to choose that song next Sunday?

Yes, I will ask him and see what he says about that idea, she smiled to herself. She decided to wait until her grandparents were ready to leave. She followed Grandpa out the door and as he walked across the porch, she quickly stepped up next to him. “Grandpa,” she asked. “Do you think you could lead the song ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ this next Sunday? I would really like to sing it again!” She felt suddenly shy at having asked such a question, and she ducked back toward the doorway of the house.

Grandpa smiled down at her. “I think I can do that. Is that a song you like?” His eyes twinkled at Ellie. “I’ll be happy to lead that one just for you.”

Ellie could scarcely wait for church the following Sunday. She would get to sing “her” song. Grandpa said he would choose it and she had no doubt he would do as he said.

Sunday morning, she waited eagerly for the song service to begin. The first and second songs were ones that were not familiar to her. Then came time for the third one. “Let’s sing number 8 in the Appendix,” announced the song leader. Ellie’s heart sang. They were going to sing her favorite song. Her grandpa had honored her request. Her eyes shone as she joined in the singing of the beautiful song. It was a lovely hymn that spoke of Jesus’ care as a Shepherd and a Friend, and how He would always keep His children close to Himself.

Later, after church was over and they were on their way home, Ellie remarked to her mother, “Grandpa chose that one song, just like I asked him to!”

Ellie’s mom looked a bit startled. “You asked him to lead a song today? When did you ask him?”

“Yes, I did. The other evening when they visited, I asked him if he could lead it today and he said he would. And he did!” Ellie said with delight.

Mom had a strange look on her face, and she was quiet for a moment.

“Did you know that Grandpas weren’t there today? At the last minute they decided to visit elsewhere this morning for church.” Mom smiled tenderly at her little daughter. “It seems that God knew what a little girl’s heart was desiring and He led another brother to choose the song you like so much. That’s so amazing, isn’t it?” Ellie nodded. To think that Grandpa wasn’t even at church today, and still they sang her favorite song anyway! It gave her such a special feeling to know that Jesus cared for her that much.

Today, Ellie is a grown-up woman and now has children of her own. Whenever she thinks about how Jesus cares for all His children, she especially remembers how God cared about one little, five-year-old girl and the song she loved so much. As her mother said, and still does, “Of course God cares. He loves all the little children of the world!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

Ellie aproximou sua cadeira mais dos adultos que visitavam a cozinha. Vovô, vovó e tia Lily tinham passado para uma visita, e embora ela nem sempre compreendesse a conversa, adorava ouvir. Descobria que aprendia muitas coisas desse jeito.

O assunto daquela noite dizia respeito a algo relacionado à igreja e isso fez sua mente pensar sobre cantar durante os cultos da manhã de domingo. Embora Ellie tivesse apenas cinco anos, gostava muito de cantar. Pensou no fato de que seu querido avô era líder de cânticos na igreja deles e em como gostava quando ele conduzia um hino.

Na igreja de Ellie, os condutores de cânticos sentavam-se todos ao redor de uma mesa perto do centro da igreja. Eles se revezavam escolhendo um canto e então o conduziam para a congregação. Ellie nem sempre conhecia as músicas escolhidas. Cantavam de um pequeno hinário preto que tinha muitas canções com palavras difíceis e melodias que ela não reconhecia. Porém, na parte de trás desse pequeno hinário havia uma seção chamada “O Apêndice” e ali estavam hinos que lhe eram familiares, e ela ficava sempre satisfeita quando um canto era anunciado dessa parte do livro. Seu hino favorito era “Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us” e, embora ainda não soubesse ler, ela sabia que era o número oito. Quando aquele número de hino era anunciado numa manhã de domingo, ela sempre sentia um formigamento de excitação. Eu vou poder ajudar neste canto!

Tomara que cantássemos esse hino de novo, pensou Ellie. Faz tanto tempo que não cantamos.

Então um pensamento súbito lhe ocorreu. Por que eu não poderia pedir ao vovô para escolher esse hino no próximo domingo?

Sim, vou pedir a ele e ver o que ele acha dessa ideia, sorriu para si mesma. Decidiu esperar até que seus avós estivessem prontos para ir embora. Seguiu o vovô até a porta e, enquanto ele atravessava a varanda, ela rapidamente se colocou ao lado dele. “Vovô,” perguntou. “Você acha que poderia conduzir o hino ‘Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ neste próximo domingo? Eu gostaria muito de cantá-lo de novo!” Sentiu-se de repente tímida por ter feito tal pedido, e recuou em direção à entrada da casa.

O vovô sorriu para ela. “Acho que posso fazer isso. É um hino que você gosta?” Seus olhos brilharam para Ellie. “Ficarei feliz em conduzir esse só para você.”

Ellie mal podia esperar pelo culto dominical seguinte. Ela iria cantar “seu” hino. O vovô disse que o escolheria e ela não duvidou que ele faria como prometera.

No domingo de manhã, esperou ansiosa pelo início do momento de cânticos. O primeiro e o segundo hinos não lhe eram familiares. Então chegou a hora do terceiro. “Vamos cantar o número 8 do Apêndice,” anunciou o líder de cânticos. O coração de Ellie cantou. Irão cantar seu hino preferido. Seu avô havia atendido ao seu pedido. Seus olhos brilharam enquanto ela se juntava ao canto do belo hino. Era um hino encantador que falava do cuidado de Jesus como Pastor e Amigo, e de como Ele manteria sempre Seus filhos perto de Si.

Mais tarde, depois do culto, a caminho de casa, Ellie comentou com a mãe: “O vovô escolheu aquele hino, exatamente como eu pedi!”

A mãe de Ellie pareceu um pouco surpresa. “Você pediu a ele para conduzir um hino hoje? Quando você o pediu?”

“Sim, eu pedi. Outro dia quando vieram nos visitar, perguntei se ele poderia conduzi-lo hoje e ele disse que sim. E ele o fez!” disse Ellie, encantada.

A mãe teve uma expressão estranha no rosto, e ficou em silêncio por um momento.

“Você sabia que os avós não estavam aqui hoje? No último minuto decidiram visitar outro lugar esta manhã para o culto.” A mãe sorriu ternamente para a filha pequena. “Parece que Deus soube o desejo do coração de uma menininha e Ele conduziu outro irmão a escolher o hino de que você tanto gosta. Não é maravilhoso?” Ellie assentiu. Pensar que o vovô nem sequer estava na igreja hoje, e ainda assim cantaram seu hino preferido! Isso lhe dava uma sensação tão especial saber que Jesus se importava tanto com ela.

Hoje, Ellie é uma mulher adulta e tem agora filhos seus. Sempre que pensa em como Jesus cuida de todos os Seus filhos, lembra-se especialmente de como Deus cuidou de uma menininha de cinco anos e do hino de que ela tanto gostava. Como sua mãe disse, e ainda diz, “Claro que Deus se importa. Ele ama todas as criancinhas do mundo!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

Ellie flyttade sin stol närmare de vuxna som var på besök i köket. Farfar, farmor och moster Lily hade tittat in, och även om hon inte alltid förstod samtalet tyckte hon om att lyssna. Hon upptäckte att hon lärde sig mycket på det viset.

Ämnet den här kvällen handlade om något i kyrkan och det fick henne att tänka på sång under söndagsgudstjänsterna. Fastän Ellie bara var fem år gammal älskade hon verkligen att sjunga. Hon tänkte på att hennes käre farfar var sångledare i deras församling och hur mycket hon tyckte om när han ledde en sång.

I Ellies kyrka satt sångledarna runt ett bord nära mitten av kyrksalen. De turades om att välja en sång och sedan leda den för församlingen. Ellie kände inte alltid igen de sånger som valdes. De sjöng ur en liten svart sångbok som hade många sånger med svåra ord och melodier hon inte kände igen. Men längst bak i den här lilla sångboken fanns en sektion som hette ”Appendixen” och där fanns psalmer som var bekanta för henne, och hon blev alltid glad när en sång meddelades från den delen av boken. Hennes favoritsång var ’Saviour, Like a Shepherd Lead Us’ och även om hon inte kunde läsa ännu visste hon att den var nummer åtta. När just det sångnumret meddelades en söndag morgon kände hon alltid en pirrande förväntan. Jag kommer att kunna hjälpa till med den här sången!

Jag önskar att vi skulle sjunga den sången igen, tänkte Ellie. Det var länge sen vi gjorde det.

Så fick hon plötsligt en tanke. Varför kunde hon inte be farfar välja den sången nästa söndag?

Ja, jag ska fråga honom och se vad han säger om den idén, log hon för sig själv. Hon bestämde sig för att vänta tills hennes morföräldrar var redo att gå. Hon följde efter farfar ut genom dörren och när han gick över verandan klev hon snabbt upp bredvid honom. ”Farfar,” frågade hon. ”Tror du att du kan leda sången ’Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us’ nästa söndag? Jag skulle verkligen vilja sjunga den igen!” Hon blev plötsligt blyg för att ha ställt en sådan fråga och kröp tillbaka mot dörröppningen till huset.

Farfar log ner mot henne. ”Jag tror att jag kan göra det. Är det en sång du tycker om?” Hans ögon glittrade mot Ellie. ”Jag ska gärna leda den bara för dig.”

Ellie kunde knappt vänta till gudstjänsten nästa söndag. Hon skulle få sjunga ”sin” sång. Farfar hade sagt att han skulle välja den och hon tvivlade inte på att han skulle göra som han sagt.

Söndag morgon väntade hon ivrigt på att sångstunden skulle börja. Den första och andra sången var sådana hon inte kände igen. Sedan var det dags för den tredje. ”Låt oss sjunga nummer 8 i Appendixen,” meddelade sångledaren. Ellies hjärta sjöng. De skulle sjunga hennes favoritsång. Hennes farfar hade hållit sitt löfte. Hennes ögon tindrade när hon gick med i sången. Det var en vacker psalm som talade om Jesu omsorg som en herde och en vän, och hur Han alltid skulle hålla sina barn nära sig.

Senare, efter gudstjänsten när de var på väg hem, sade Ellie till sin mamma: ”Farfar valde den där sången, precis som jag bad honom göra!”

Ellies mamma såg lite förvånad ut. ”Du bad honom leda en sång idag? När frågade du honom?”

”Ja, det gjorde jag. En kväll när de var på besök frågade jag honom om han kunde leda den idag och han sa att han skulle. Och det gjorde han!” sade Ellie lyckligt.

Mamman hade ett märkligt uttryck i ansiktet och hon blev tyst en stund.

”Visste du att farfar inte var där idag? I sista stund bestämde de sig för att besöka en annan plats den här morgonen för gudstjänsten.” Mamman log ömt mot sin lilla dotter. ”Det verkar som om Gud visste vad ett litet hjärta längtade efter och ledde en annan broder att välja den sång du tycker så mycket om. Visst är det underbart?” Ellie nickade. Att tänka att farfar inte ens var i kyrkan idag, och ändå sjöng de hennes favoritsång! Det gav henne en så särskild känsla att veta att Jesus brydde sig så mycket om henne.

Idag är Ellie vuxen och har egna barn. Närhelst hon tänker på hur Jesus tar hand om alla sina barn minns hon särskilt hur Gud brydde sig om en liten femårig flicka och sången hon älskade så mycket. Som hennes mamma sade, och fortfarande säger, ”Självklart bryr sig Gud. Han älskar världens alla små barn!”

Saviour, Like A Shepherd Lead Us

When you, my friend, are standing on this earth
And gazing up into the firmament
Where stretches all of space, what do you see?
A great black blanket stretched o’er all the sky
With many a mystery light somewhere up there?
Or can you see the distances so great
Which stretch the mind almost to breaking point
And make you feel the size you really are?
In the still silence of the spacious sky,
The far-off planets seem almost in reach
Compared to the great distance to the stars.
The crescent moon is closer yet to you,
And yet it took man three whole days to reach
That tiny sphere so very close at hand.
But what you see while gazing up to heights
Which you cannot begin to comprehend
Is but a streak of all the vast expanse
Beyond the knowledge of this human race.
And so, my friend, I hope that you will feel
That greatness, vastness, emptiness of space
Which our Creator made for us so we
Can feel His greatness and His tender love
And humbly bow our heads and worship Him.

–by Daniel Kaufman
